classification.difficultyReason: Combine two graphical comparisons and distinguish included and excluded endpoints.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=|x-2|$, $y=1$ and $y=3$. Find the intersection coordinates:
$$\begin{align*}x-2&=-1\\x&=1\\x-2&=1\\x&=3\\x-2&=-3\\x&=-1\\x-2&=3\\x&=5\end{align*}$$
The curve is on or above $y=1$ when $x\le1$ or $x\ge3$. It is below $y=3$ when $-1<x<5$.
Combining these regions gives $-1<x\le1$ or $3\le x<5$.

spec.description: Absolute-value graph with comparison levels 1 and 3; filled endpoints at height 1 and open endpoints at height 3.
spec.mathematics: Vertex (2,0); intersections with y=1 at x=1,3 and y=3 at x=-1,5.
